description: The item schema (docs/format-schema.md, draft 3): field names and shapes, positions, builders, the view (previous passwords, dates, deleting), unknown fields, moving an item, and the settings item. Expectations are written by hand from the schema's sentences; where a sentence leaves a choice, the description of the vector says which reading was taken.

vectors.description: The position at the end is after every existing one, however they are listed.

vectors.name: schema/web/two-devices-add-offline-both-survive
vectors.description: Two devices each add a website while offline, with different ids: after both sync, both are there, in position order.

vectors.name: schema/web/two-devices-add-offline-same-position
vectors.description: Two devices each add a website at the same position: both survive, ordered by field name (the smaller id first), whatever order the writes arrive in.

vectors.name: schema/web/same-position-three-entries-by-field-name
vectors.description: Three websites at one position are shown in order of field name.

vectors.name: schema/web/reorder-by-position
vectors.description: Moving one website between two others is one write of that website with a new position; the others are not written.

vectors.name: schema/web/reorder-on-two-devices-later-write-wins
vectors.description: The same website moved on two devices: the later write of the whole value wins, address and position together.

vectors.name: schema/web/removed-on-one-device-edited-on-another
vectors.description: One device removes a website while another edits it: the later write wins, as for any field.

vectors.name: schema/tag/added-twice-with-the-same-text-shows-once
vectors.description: Two devices add the same tag text: two fields, one tag.

vectors.name: schema/tag/removed-after-two-adds-clears-both-fields
vectors.description: Removing a tag clears every field that holds its text: the tag is gone.

vectors.name: schema/tag/remove-sees-only-one-of-two-fields
vectors.description: A device that had only one of the two fields clears that one: the other still holds the text, and the tag is shown (a limit of the schema, in the findings).

vectors.name: schema/tag/order-is-bytewise-by-text
vectors.description: Tags have no position: they are shown in order of their text, bytewise (the schema says nothing).

vectors.name: schema/tag/order-is-utf8-a-character-above-ffff-after-one-in-e000-to-ffff
vectors.description: Tags are ordered bytewise as UTF-8 (draft 3). U+E000 is EE 80 80 and U+10000 is F0 90 80 80, so the one above U+FFFF comes last; in JavaScript string order (UTF-16) U+10000 is the surrogate pair D800 DC00 and would come first.

vectors.name: schema/tag/order-is-utf8-three-characters
vectors.description: The same with U+FFFF (EF BF BF) between them, and plain ASCII before all: ASCII, U+E000, U+FFFF, U+10000.

vectors.name: schema/field/f/label-and-value-change-on-two-devices-one-unit
vectors.description: A custom field is one value. One device changes its label and another, later, changes its value: the later write is the whole field and the label change is lost.

vectors.name: schema/field/f/later-label-change-wins-over-earlier-value-change
vectors.description: The same two writes the other way round: the later one is the label change.

vectors.name: schema/attachment/removed
vectors.description: Removing an attachment is a clear of its field.

vectors.name: schema/card/reissued-new-number-and-code
vectors.description: A reissued card: the number, expiry and code are written again. The old number is not shown anywhere, and a checkpoint carries one write of card and none of the old (only password keeps history).

vectors.name: schema/card/reissued-code-cleared
vectors.description: A reissued card with no printed code: the code is cleared.

vectors.name: schema/password/twelve-changes-show-ten
vectors.description: Thirteen writes of password (twelve changes): the current one is p12, and the ten newest earlier ones are shown newest first, each dated by the write that replaced it. p1 and p0 are not shown. Each change names the write it replaced, so there is no note.

vectors.name: schema/password/checkpoint-keeps-ten-earlier-writes
vectors.description: A checkpoint of those thirteen writes carries the winner and the writes the first ten entries need: here the ten entries themselves (11 writes with the winner). A reader of the checkpoint alone shows the same ten previous passwords as a reader of every record.

vectors.name: schema/password/checkpoint-then-two-more-changes
vectors.description: A checkpoint of the first thirteen writes and then two more records: the view is the one of all fifteen records (ten newest previous: p13 down to p4).

vectors.name: schema/password/previous-must-differ
vectors.description: The same password written again is not a previous password: p1, p1, p2 shows p1 once: the first write is followed by the same value and is not an entry; the second is, and is dated by the write that replaced it (3000).

vectors.name: schema/password/entry-equal-to-a-newer-entry-is-left-out
vectors.description: p1, p2, p1, p3: the oldest p1 equals a newer entry and is left out; newest first the list is p1 (replaced at 4000) and p2 (replaced at 3000).

vectors.name: schema/password/restore-is-a-new-write
vectors.description: Restoring a previous password sets password to that value. The password it replaces becomes the newest previous one; the restored value is the current password, so it is not listed again.

vectors.name: schema/password/cleared-write-is-not-an-entry
vectors.description: A cleared password in between is not an entry; the write before it is dated by the clear that replaced it (2000), and there is no note: the second change names the clear as the write it replaced.

vectors.name: schema/password/checkpoint-keeps-the-write-that-dates-an-entry
vectors.description: The same, through a checkpoint: it carries the cleared write too (it dates p1 and is the write the winner replaced), so the list and the absence of a note do not change.

vectors.name: schema/password/history-from-an-import-follows-the-writes
vectors.description: password_history (from an import) follows the entries from writes.

vectors.name: schema/password/import-entry-equal-to-a-write-is-left-out
vectors.description: An entry of password_history equal to an entry from writes (or to the current password) is left out.

vectors.name: schema/password/import-history-and-writes-limited-to-ten
vectors.description: Eight entries from writes and four entries of password_history: ten are shown, the writes first, then two from the import.

vectors.name: schema/password/shown-before-clearing
vectors.description: Three writes and an imported entry: the control for the next vector.

vectors.name: schema/password/after-clear-previous-passwords
vectors.description: Clear Previous Passwords sets history_hidden (1) and clears password_history. Of the writes of password before the clearing record, all but the last (p3) are left out, and p3 is the current password, so nothing is listed. The earlier writes are still in the records.

vectors.name: schema/password/change-after-clear-shows-the-current-one-of-the-time
vectors.description: A change after clearing: the password that was current when the history was cleared is now replaced and is listed (draft 2); the ones before it stay hidden.

vectors.name: schema/password/second-change-after-clear
vectors.description: A second change after clearing: p4 and p3 are listed, p2 and p1 are not.

vectors.name: schema/password/checkpoint-after-clear-no-longer-carries-hidden-writes
vectors.description: A checkpoint written after Clear Previous Passwords carries only the writes in force: p5, p4 and p3. The earlier writes leave storage with the records the checkpoint covers; the view does not change.

vectors.name: schema/password/restore-after-clear
vectors.description: Restoring a hidden password writes it again after the place: it is current, and the one it replaces (p3) is listed.

vectors.name: schema/password/stale-device-clears-later-and-hides-the-same
vectors.description: Device A clears after seeing p3. Device B had not yet seen p3 and clears later by the clock. Draft 2 kept a place in the value and the older place brought p2 back; now the later clearing hides all but the last write before it, which is p3, and nothing comes back.

vectors.name: schema/password/earlier-clearing-arriving-late-changes-nothing
vectors.description: A clearing that is earlier in the order than the winning one (here by a device that arrives last) is not the winner: the same view as with the later one alone.

vectors.name: schema/password/later-clearing-also-hides-what-came-after-the-first
vectors.description: A cleared, then changed the password to p4, then B (later by the clock) cleared: B's clearing is the winner, so only p4, the last write before it, remains and p3 is hidden too.

vectors.name: schema/password/clearing-in-the-middle-of-the-writes
vectors.description: A clearing whose place is between p3 and a later p4: p3 is the last write before it and is kept, so p3 is listed once p4 replaced it; p1 and p2 are hidden.

vectors.name: schema/password/clearing-arriving-after-a-checkpoint-hides-the-same
vectors.description: A checkpoint of p1 to p4, then a clearing that sits between p3 and p4 arrives from a device that was offline: the view is the same as folding every record, and the checkpoint alone (without the clearing) still lists p3, p2 and p1.

vectors.name: schema/password/history-hidden-of-the-wrong-shape-counts-as-cleared
vectors.description: A later write of history_hidden whose value is not 1 is the winner and is treated as cleared (schema 1): nothing is hidden and p2 and p1 are listed again. No writer produces this; it is the one way a clearing is undone.

vectors.name: schema/password/two-devices-from-the-same-base-note
vectors.description: Two devices change the password from the same base: the later write wins and the other is the newest previous password. The winner names the base as the write it replaced, but the write just before it in the order is the other change: the note.

vectors.name: schema/password/sequential-changes-no-note
vectors.description: Three sequential changes: each names the write just before it. No note.

vectors.name: schema/password/third-change-after-both-were-seen-no-note
vectors.description: A third change made after both of the two were seen names the winner of the two as the write it replaced: no note.

vectors.name: schema/password/null-over-with-an-earlier-write-note
vectors.description: A device that saw no password writes one (over null) while another write already exists before it in the order: the note.

vectors.name: schema/password/first-write-over-null-no-note
vectors.description: The first write of password has nothing before it: no note.

vectors.name: schema/password/record-without-password-over-no-note
vectors.description: A record that changes password without password_over (an older writer): the reader cannot tell what that device had seen and shows no note.

vectors.name: schema/password/password-over-of-an-earlier-record-no-note
vectors.description: A later write of password without password_over, after one that had it: the winning password_over is not from the same record, so it says nothing about this write.

vectors.name: schema/password/password-over-of-the-wrong-shape-no-note
vectors.description: password_over of the wrong shape counts as cleared: no note.

vectors.name: schema/password/two-devices-note-after-a-cleared-write-needs-the-clear
vectors.description: base, a clear, then a change that names the clear: no note (the write just before the winner is the clear).

vectors.name: schema/password/two-devices-note-through-a-checkpoint
vectors.description: The two-devices case, and the sequential case, through a checkpoint alone and through a checkpoint and the records after it: the same note or none. A checkpoint keeps password_over (the winner of every field) and the write just before the winner.

vectors.name: schema/password/sequential-note-through-a-checkpoint-with-a-write-before-the-winner-that-is-no-entry
vectors.description: p1, then p2 three times in a row, each naming the one before: the write just before the winner is not an entry (it repeats the winner) and dates no entry, yet a checkpoint keeps it, so there is still no note.

vectors.name: schema/password/checkpoint-keeps-the-write-that-divides-hidden-from-shown
vectors.description: p1 at 2000 is the last write of password before the clearing at 2500, so it divides what is hidden from what is shown; it repeats the next write (p1 at 3000) and so is no entry and dates none. The checkpoint (of everything but the late write) must still keep it: when p3 from a device that was offline arrives, sorted at 1500 before the divider, it stays hidden. Without the divider p3 would take its place and be listed.

vectors.name: schema/dates/made-here
vectors.description: An item made here: Added is created, Edited is the wall time of the latest write to a content field.

vectors.name: schema/dates/no-created-added-is-the-earliest-write-held
vectors.description: An item without created (an old writer): Added is the wall time of the earliest write the reader holds, and the view says it is an estimate: it can drift once a checkpoint has dropped older writes.

vectors.name: schema/dates/imported-untouched
vectors.description: An imported item untouched: the source's dates are shown, although every write was made at import time (9000).

vectors.name: schema/dates/imported-edited-later
vectors.description: An imported item edited later here: Edited is the time of that write.

vectors.name: schema/dates/imported-then-source-set-again
vectors.description: A second import that sets source and edited again does not make the item newer than the source says: edited is the value of edited when no content field was written later.

vectors.name: schema/dates/imported-without-dates-shows-added-alone
vectors.description: An item imported from a source with no dates: created is the import time and there is no edited. The latest content write is the import itself, which is not later than Added, so Edited is not shown (draft 2).

vectors.name: schema/dates/edited-equal-to-added-is-not-shown
vectors.description: Edited is shown only when later than Added: a content write at the same time as created shows no Edited.

vectors.name: schema/dates/edited-older-than-added-is-not-shown
vectors.description: An imported edited date older than created (an inconsistent source) is not shown.

vectors.name: schema/dates/only-non-content-writes
vectors.description: An item with only created, edited, source: no content write, so edited stands and Added is created.

vectors.name: schema/dates/unknown-fixed-field-is-not-content
vectors.description: An unknown fixed field written later is not a content field: it does not change Edited.

vectors.name: schema/dates/unknown-repeated-field-is-not-content
vectors.description: Nor is an unknown repeated field (draft 2: the content fields are listed): Edited does not change.

vectors.name: schema/dates/bookkeeping-fields-are-not-content
vectors.description: password_over, moved_from, history_hidden, source, edited and created written later do not change Edited.

vectors.name: schema/dates/a-clear-is-a-write-to-a-content-field
vectors.description: A clear of a content field is a write to it.

vectors.name: schema/dates/wrong-shape-edited-falls-back
vectors.description: edited of the wrong shape counts as cleared: Edited is the latest content write.

vectors.name: schema/deleted/control-no-later-write
vectors.description: deleted after every other write: the item is in Recently Deleted.

vectors.name: schema/deleted/second-import-sets-source-stays-deleted
vectors.description: A second import sets source again after the item was deleted: source is not a content field, so the item stays deleted.

vectors.name: schema/deleted/second-import-sets-edited-and-created-stays-deleted
vectors.description: A later write of edited and created does not bring the item back.

vectors.name: schema/deleted/history-hidden-later-stays-deleted
vectors.description: Clear Previous Passwords (history_hidden) after the delete does not bring the item back.

vectors.name: schema/deleted/password-over-and-moved-from-later-stay-deleted
vectors.description: password_over and moved_from are not content fields.

vectors.name: schema/deleted/content-edit-brings-it-back
vectors.description: A later write to a content field brings the item back.

vectors.name: schema/deleted/clear-of-content-field-brings-it-back
vectors.description: A later clear of a content field is an edit too.

vectors.name: schema/deleted/edit-before-the-delete-stays-deleted
vectors.description: A content write earlier than deleted in the order does not bring the item back.

vectors.name: schema/deleted/unknown-fixed-field-later-stays-deleted
vectors.description: An unknown fixed field written after the delete is not a content field: the item stays deleted, and Edited does not change.

vectors.name: schema/deleted/unknown-repeated-field-later-stays-deleted
vectors.description: An unknown repeated field written after the delete is not a content field either (draft 2): the item stays deleted, and Edited does not change.

vectors.name: schema/deleted/deleted-cleared
vectors.description: Clearing deleted restores the item.

vectors.name: schema/unknown/kept-through-a-checkpoint
vectors.description: A field of a later version (a fixed name and a repeated one) is never shown, never cleared by this version, and kept: a checkpoint carries one write of each, and the view of the checkpoint alone lists them.

vectors.name: schema/unknown/other-keys-in-a-known-map-are-kept-and-ignored
vectors.description: A known field whose map has keys the schema does not define keeps working: the extra key is kept and ignored.

vectors.name: schema/move/carries-the-list-of-schema-7
vectors.description: The first record sets every content field (here with a field of the wrong shape, notes, which travels) and every unknown field; created and edited from Added and Edited; moved_from; password_over null (the other group holds no copy); clears moved and deleted (the item is not deleted); a cleared field (username), password_history and history_hidden are not carried. The second record, in the old group, sets moved naming the group it went to.

vectors.name: schema/move/imported-item-keeps-dates-and-source
vectors.description: An imported item moved: created and edited are the source's dates (shown as before), and source is carried so that a second import still finds the item.

vectors.name: schema/move/deleted-item-stays-deleted
vectors.description: An item that is in Recently Deleted when moved: deleted is set in the first record, and the item arrives deleted (nothing in that record is later than it). It is not cleared.

vectors.name: schema/move/deleted-then-edited-arrives-not-deleted
vectors.description: An item deleted, then edited (so it is back), then moved: deleted is still a field of the item, but the item is not in Recently Deleted, so it is cleared in the first record and the item arrives not deleted.

vectors.name: schema/move/back-clears-moved-and-the-content-fields-the-copy-has
vectors.description: Moving it back to the group it left, which still holds the old copy marked moved: the first record clears moved, and also every content field the old copy has and the item no longer has (notes), so that nothing stale comes back (draft 3). The copy has no password, so password_over is null.

vectors.name: schema/move/arrival-names-the-password-the-group-already-holds
vectors.description: The group the item goes to already holds a copy with a password (written at 1000 by device 1 of author A, seq 1). password_over is the place of that winning write, so the arrival is not taken for a change on two devices. The copy also has a website the item does not: cleared; and a field a later version wrote (not content): left alone.

vectors.name: schema/move/there-and-back-with-the-password-unchanged
vectors.description: The item was made in group 1 (password p1 written at 1000), moved to group 2 and is now moved back, the password unchanged. Group 1 still holds the old copy marked moved. The arrival names the winning password write of that copy, so there is no note, and p1 written again is not a previous password.

vectors.name: schema/move/there-and-back-with-the-password-changed
vectors.description: The same, with the password changed to p2 while the item was in group 2 (the change names the arrival write as the one it replaced). Moving back writes p2 in group 1 over the old p1 write there: no note, and p1 is the newest previous password, dated by the arrival (60000).

vectors.name: schema/classify/moved-completed
vectors.description: Group 2 holds the arrived copy (moved_from names group 1) and group 1 has moved, naming group 2, later than that: the move is complete.

vectors.name: schema/classify/interrupted-after-the-first-write
vectors.description: Group 2 holds the arrived copy and group 1 has no moved: the first record was written and the second was not. The device that wrote the first finishes with moved in group 1.

vectors.name: schema/classify/interrupted-and-edited-in-the-target
vectors.description: The arrived copy was edited before the second record: still an interrupted move (the rule does not look at the content).

vectors.name: schema/classify/an-older-moved-is-no-completion
vectors.description: Group 1 carries a moved from an earlier trip that is older than the arrival: it is not the second record of this move: in progress.

vectors.name: schema/classify/moved-to-a-third-group-is-no-completion
vectors.description: Group 1 moved the item later, but to a third group: not the second record of the move to group 2.

vectors.name: schema/classify/same-item-id-without-moved-from-is-separate
vectors.description: The same item_id and the same content in two groups, and no moved_from from one to the other: two separate items.

vectors.name: schema/classify/moved-from-names-a-third-group-is-separate
vectors.description: The copy in group 2 came from a third group: not from group 1: two separate items.

vectors.name: schema/classify/moved-without-moved-from-is-separate
vectors.description: Group 1 is marked moved towards group 2 but the copy there has no moved_from (written by something else): no move is recognised.

vectors.name: schema/classify/there-and-back-completed
vectors.description: Moved to group 2 and back: both copies carry moved_from naming the other; the later one (group 1, which also cleared moved) says the item last went to group 1, and group 2 has moved, naming group 1, later: complete, from group 2 to group 1.

vectors.name: schema/classify/back-interrupted-after-the-first-write
vectors.description: The same, and the device stopped after the first record of the way back: group 2 is not marked: in progress from group 2 to group 1.

vectors.name: schema/settings/name-and-gone-entry
vectors.description: The settings item holds the group's name and gone/id entries for imported items deleted for good.

vectors.name: schema/settings/name-written-on-two-devices-later-wins
vectors.description: The name merges like any field: the later write wins.

vectors.name: schema/settings/gone-entry-cleared
vectors.description: A gone entry can be cleared (the person imports the item again on purpose).

vectors.name: schema/settings/gone-entry-with-the-wrong-id-is-invalid
vectors.description: A gone/id whose id is not the hash of its kind and id is of the wrong shape: treated as cleared and kept.

vectors.name: schema/settings/name-of-the-wrong-shape
vectors.description: name that is not text counts as cleared.

vectors.name: schema/settings/unknown-fields-and-item-fields-are-kept-not-shown
vectors.description: In the settings item, a field the schema does not define for it (an item field such as title, a later version's field) is kept and not shown.

vectors.name: schema/settings/two-gone-entries-in-order
vectors.description: gone entries are listed in order of their field names.

vectors.name: schema/settings/name-is-not-normalised-by-the-reader
vectors.description: The reader shows the name as written: a writer normalises, a reader does not change what it finds.

vectors.name: schema/size/reader-shows-a-title-over-the-limit
vectors.description: A reader shows a text of 65,537 bytes it finds: the limit binds the writer only.

vectors.name: schema/size/reader-shows-notes-over-the-limit
vectors.description: A reader shows notes of 262,145 bytes.

vectors.name: schema/size/reader-shows-65-websites-count
vectors.description: A reader shows all 65 websites it finds: sixty-five entries in the view, all at one position and so in order of field name.

vectors.name: schema/size/reader-shows-65-tags
vectors.description: And 65 tags, in order of their text.

vectors.name: schema/sealed/two-devices-each-add-a-website
vectors.description: Sealed records of a group with two writers. Alice makes the login with one website; then alice on one device and bob on another each add a website at the same wall time without having seen the other's. After the group reader accepted every record, the item shows all three websites in order of position (i, ia, j), Added is the created of the first record and Edited the time of the latest write to a content field.

vectors.name: schema/sealed/previous-passwords-across-a-checkpoint
vectors.description: Alice changes the password three times, a manager (bob) seals a checkpoint that restates the winning writes and the history the schema keeps for Previous Passwords and covers alice's chain, and alice changes it once more. Read twice: with every record, and after the three covered records were deleted from storage (the checkpoint alone carries them). The item shows p4 and the three earlier passwords newest first, each dated by the write that replaced it, and no note, in both.

vectors.name: schema/sealed/move-there-and-back
vectors.description: An item made in group 1, moved to group 2, its password changed there, and moved back: sealed records of both groups. In group 1 the item is shown again with the new password, the old one as the newest previous password (dated by the arrival), no note (the arrival names the password write the old copy there still holds), Added from created and Edited from the change made in group 2. In group 2 the item is hidden, marked moved to group 1.
